text: All of the triangles in the diagram below are similar to isosceles triangle $ABC$, in which $AB = AC$. Each of the $7$ smallest triangles has area $1$, and $\triangle ABC$ has area $40$. What is the area of trapezoid $DBCE$?
figure: Isosceles triangle ABC with apex A at the top and base BC horizontal at the bottom. Point D is on side AB and point E is on side AC, with segment DE parallel to BC (about halfway down from A to BC). Just above DE is a thin strip between DE and a shorter horizontal segment whose ends lie on AB and AC. The strip is cut by a zigzag into 7 small congruent triangles: 4 pointing up, whose bases lie side by side along DE and fill it from D to E, and 3 pointing down between them, whose bases lie along the top segment. The top segment is 3 small bases long. Trapezoid DBCE is the region below DE.
